## Historical audit — S0142, visible chunk 2 of 5

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/generic_rsi/C1/development/commons_109923183/trajectory.jsonl`. All citations below refer to this file. The reference and render images themselves are not visible in the supplied observations.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| **Goal and first build** — student `model_request`, line 7, characters [0,257753) | The task requested a 3D reconstruction of one indoor photograph, matching camera, framing, occlusion and colors. The student’s code interpreted the scene as a paneled room with parquet, chaise, foreground cane chair and curtains. These object identifications are the student’s interpretation, not independently verified image content. |
| **Geometry and materials** — line 7, [0,257753); student `model_response`, line 9, [0,13641) | Both programs define multiple assemblies and separate chaise rails, legs, arms, upholstery and pillow, plus procedural stripe and bump materials. The revision attempts to rotate the chaise and parent extra upholstery to it. Grouping and coordinates show intended part relationships, but do not establish physical contact, correct pose or visual fidelity. |
| **First validation** — line 7, [0,257753) | Feedback reports step 1 `ok: true`, a completed 16-sample render and saved image; the next request includes both reference and render paths. This establishes reported execution/render success, not a verified match. |
| **Student diagnosis and revision** — lines 8–10, respectively [0,3363), [0,13641), [0,14297) | In a fresh read-only session with two images supplied and zero recorded tool calls, the student estimated chaise width at 49% versus a target of 79%, and reported sloping moldings, a low floor boundary, pale tones and insufficient foreground crop. These are student observations, not independently checked here. The revised code moves and redirects the camera while retaining the lens, moves the wall, rotates the chaise, darkens materials and lighting, adjusts the chair and pillow, and adds chair legs. Line 10 records execution of that program; its result is not visible in this chunk. |

**Teacher input and autonomy.** No teacher message, teacher diagnosis, or teacher-proposed update is visible. The feedback request to compare the render is runner input, not evidence of teacher advice or adoption. The student independently produced a diagnosis and revision within the shown session; no separate exploratory tool calls are recorded (lines 7–9).

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Step 1 has reported technical success; overall task correctness and step 2’s outcome are **unknown**. There is no visible formal success assessment, algorithm failure, empty patch or technical interruption. Neither image can be inspected here, so camera alignment, lighting, rendered textures, occlusions, object pose and part connections remain unverified. The student’s proposed fixes may improve or worsen the match; the recorded execution alone does not resolve that hypothesis.

**Lessons.** Transferable process: distinguish reported render completion from visual validation, and test camera-wide discrepancies separately from local object changes. Task-specific hypotheses are the particular width estimates, wall placement, chaise rotation and darker palette; none is independently established by this excerpt.
